Supersedes the inherited 'Claude is the only worker that edits code' line, which was stricter than the playbook's own section 4. Claude still edits by default; any worker may edit named work the operator explicitly authorizes; permission is never self-certifying (a worker claiming it does not have it); non-Claude code still gets a Claude line-by-line review before merge; and permission to edit is never permission to widen authority or weaken a gate.

subject: sprint
text: Sprint 2026-08-26: the Core is now the PC-side half of the intercom. aletheia/sync.py (git pull/rebase/push with retry, honest degradation) + core_tick loop: pull commands, execute PC-only kinds, push receipts + journal. New intercom kinds browse_read/browse_shot with a STATIC cloud/local partition so a command has exactly one possible executor - no races between Actions and the Core by construction. Command Center now renders the grammar from /api/kinds instead of its own copy, which had already drifted. 21 new tests, all against a real local bare repo. Voice-to-PC-browser now needs exactly one thing: the Core running.

subject: sprint
text: Sprint 2026-08-26b: Aletheia becomes always-on and self-updating. aletheia/supervisor.py relaunches the Core - immediately on a self-update exit (code 42), with bounded doubling backoff on a crash, hidden at-logon Scheduled Task via 'supervisor install'. core_tick now detects pulled commits touching CODE_PATHS and restarts the Core onto the new code, so a merge to main lands on the PC within about one sync beat with no human involved. State-only commits never restart. bootstrap.ps1/start-aletheia.bat now run the supervisor and open the wall. 9 new tests.

subject: sprint
text: Sprint 2026-08-26c, operator course-correction: 'the whole point is I open that web page and stuff happens if I talk - integrated, not a ChatGPT chat on the side.' Built voice INTO the pages: interface/voice.js gives the wall and Command Center ears (Web Speech API, the browser's own, no keys) and a mouth (speechSynthesis); POST /api/voice runs voice.interpret - deterministic mapping of 'Thea, ...' onto the same gated command grammar as every channel. Halt, resume, status, read a site aloud, screenshot, approve/deny (refuses to guess between two pending), add task, note; unmatched speech is journaled and says so, never guessed into an action. ChatGPT Voice demoted to the away-from-home channel. 15 new tests.

subject: outage
text: 2026-08-26 outage, root-caused from the operator's screenshot: the bootstrap died at the OPTIONAL browser install (his PC has Python 3.9 + pip 21, playwright's greenlet fell back to an MSVC source build and failed) and the script threw - so the REQUIRED Core never started and the wall showed connection refused. Two design faults, both fixed: (1) bootstrap now requires Python 3.10+, installs 3.12 via winget when absent, upgrades pip, installs optional deps wheels-only, and a browser-install failure WARNS and continues - optional steps can never again kill the required path; browse tests skip honestly when playwright is absent; aletheia/__init__ refuses pre-3.10 Python with words instead of syntax errors. (2) Found while tracing: a Core started without the supervisor would exit on the next code merge leaving nothing listening - now a supervised Core (env marker) exits 42 for its supervisor, an unsupervised one hands off to a detached supervisor instead of orphaning the port; supervisor install starts the task immediately; a second supervisor yields when a Core already answers.

subject: outage
text: Second failure from the operator's rerun screenshot: his clone had locally journaled lines from the old Core, git pull --ff-only aborted on them, and the bootstrap continued on STALE code (PowerShell does not stop on native exit codes). Root disease fixed, not the symptom: (1) per-writer journal files - the cloud writes journal.jsonl, the PC Core writes journal-pc.jsonl (journal.use_pc_journal at Core/supervisor start), entries() merges all writer files into one time-ordered stream, so journal git conflicts are structurally impossible; (2) core_tick commits local state BEFORE pulling so rebases always run on a clean tree, and pushes every tick so checkpoints publish without waiting for a receipt; autostash-conflict output is now detected as failure; (3) bootstrap is a true recovery tool - fetch, salvage local journal lines into journal-pc.jsonl, hard reset to origin/main, exit-code checks on every git step with clear messages.

subject: outage
text: Third failed run, root cause CallDepthOverflow: the bootstrap helper 'function Py' shadowed py.exe (PowerShell resolves function names before applications), so it recursed until the session died at the required checks. Also he caught the ten-minute window between PR23 and PR24, so the repo-healing wasn't in his script. Fixes: no wrapper functions at all - the interpreter resolves once to its .exe path (Get-Command -CommandType Application) and every call checks LASTEXITCODE explicitly; Remove-Item function:Py at script top so a stale function from an old run in the same window can't shadow anything; salvage now writes journal-pc.jsonl via .NET UTF8 no-BOM (Add-Content -Encoding utf8 writes a BOM in Windows PowerShell that would corrupt the first JSON line) and journal reads utf-8-sig; and after auto-start the script now WAITS for /api/status before opening the wall, so the operator never sees connection-refused again during setup.
